reason: Both occurrences of מְזוּזַת are singular ("the doorpost of the house", "the post of the gate").

old: But if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it shall be his until the year of liberty, and then it shall return to the prince; only his inheritance belongs to his sons; it shall be theirs.
new: But if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it shall be his until the year of liberty, and then it shall return to the prince; but as for his inheritance, it shall belong to his sons; it shall be theirs.
reason: אַךְ נַחֲלָתוֹ בָּנָיו לָהֶם תִּהְיֶה is adversative ("but his inheritance—his sons, it shall be theirs"); "only his inheritance" wrongly restricts what the sons receive.

old: This shall belong to the consecrated priests from the sons of Zadok, who guarded My charge, who did not stray when the sons of Israel strayed, just as the Levites strayed.
new: This shall belong to the consecrated priests from the sons of Zadok, who kept My charge, who did not stray when the sons of Israel strayed, just as the Levites strayed.
reason: שָׁמְרוּ מִשְׁמַרְתִּי is rendered "kept My charge" in 44:8, 44:15-16 and 40:46.

old: Then the king told Ashpenaz, the chief of his eunuchs, to bring some of the sons of Israel, both from the royal offspring and from the nobles,
new: Then the king told Ashpenaz, the chief of his eunuchs, to bring some of the sons of Israel, both from the royal seed and from the nobles,
reason: The Hebrew וּמִזֶּרַע הַמְּלוּכָה takes the edition's standard rendering "royal seed".

old: To You, God of my ancestors, I give thanks and offer praise, because You have granted me wisdom and might; and now You have informed me of what we asked from You, for You have disclosed to us the king's matter."
new: To You, God of my fathers, I give thanks and offer praise, because You have granted me wisdom and might; and now You have informed me of what we asked from You, for You have disclosed to us the king's matter."
reason: Aramaic אֱלָהּ אֲבָהָתִי is "God of my fathers", matching the edition's rendering of אָבוֹת (e.g. Ezekiel 47:14 "your fathers").

old: Accordingly Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had assigned to destroy the wise men of Babylon; he went and spoke to him like this: "Do not put the wise men of Babylon to death! Lead me into the king's presence, and I will report the interpretation to the king."
new: Accordingly Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had assigned to destroy the wise men of Babylon; he went and spoke to him like this: "Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon! Lead me into the king's presence, and I will report the interpretation to the king."
reason: אַל־תְּהוֹבֵד is the same verb (Haphel of אבד) rendered "destroy" earlier in the verse (לְהוֹבָדָה) and in 2:12.

old: At once Arioch brought Daniel in haste before the king and spoke to him like this: "I have found a man from the exiles of Judah who will inform the king of the interpretation."
new: Then Arioch brought Daniel in haste before the king and spoke to him like this: "I have found a man from the exiles of Judah who will inform the king of the interpretation."
reason: אֱדַיִן is "then"; haste is already expressed by בְּהִתְבְּהָלָה, so "At once" duplicates it.

old: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and bowed down to Daniel, and he gave orders to present to him an offering and soothing aromas.
new: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and bowed down to Daniel, and he gave orders to present to him an offering and soothing fragrances.
reason: רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ is 'soothing fragrance' in its other 33 occurrences.

old: Then the magicians, the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the astrologers came in, and I told the dream before them, yet they did not make its interpretation known to me.
new: Then the magicians, the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the diviners came in, and I told the dream before them, yet they did not make its interpretation known to me.
reason: גָּזְרַיָּא is rendered "diviners" in 2:27, 5:7 and 5:11.

old: "third in the kingdom": Aramaic talti (and talta in 5:16, 29) means "third" or "third ruler," fitting Belshazzar's historical position as co-regent under his father Nabonidus.
new: "third in the kingdom": Aramaic talti (and talta in 5:16, 29) means "third" or "third ruler."
reason: The historical claim about Nabonidus is outside commentary, not an explanation of the Aramaic תַלְתִּי.

old: And he was driven away from human beings, and his mind was made like that of the wild animals, and his dwelling was with the wild donkeys; he was fed grass like oxen, and his body was soaked with the dew of heaven, until he came to know that the Most High God rules over the kingdom of humanity and appoints whomever He wishes over it.
new: And he was driven away from human beings, and his heart was made like that of the wild animals, and his dwelling was with the wild donkeys; he was fed grass like oxen, and his body was soaked with the dew of heaven, until he came to know that the Most High God rules over the kingdom of humanity and appoints whomever He wishes over it.
reason: Aramaic לִבְבֵהּ is "his heart", as rendered in the parallel 4:16 (לְבַב חֵיוָה "the heart of an animal").

old: The Aramaic words name weights—mina, shekel, and half-minas (plural parsin, preceded by u-, "and," traditionally rendered "Upharsin")—which Daniel explains in 5:26-28 by wordplay on cognate verbs ("numbered," "weighed," "divided," using singular Peres) and the name Paras ("Persia").
new: The Aramaic words name weights—mina, shekel, and half-minas (plural parsin, preceded by u-, "and")—which Daniel explains in 5:26-28 by wordplay on cognate verbs ("numbered," "weighed," "divided," using singular Peres) and the name Paras ("Persia").
reason: Translator note should describe the Hebrew, not English translation tradition; removes the traditional English form of וּפַרְסִין.

old: Aramaic hargishu (Haphel of rgsh, also in 6:12) literally means "came thronging" or "crowded in noisily," though ancient versions often understood it as "came by agreement."
new: Aramaic hargishu (Haphel of rgsh, also in 6:12) literally means "came thronging" or "crowded in noisily"; some take it as "acted in concert."
reason: The claim about what ancient versions did is inaccurate; the note should describe the sense of הַרְגִּשׁוּ.

old: Then those men crowded in on the king and said to the king, "Know, King, that it is a law of the Medes and Persians that no ban or statute the king establishes can be changed."
new: Then those men came thronging to the king and said to the king, "Know, King, that it is a law of Media and Persia that no ban or statute the king establishes can be changed."
reason: הַרְגִּשׁוּ עַל־מַלְכָּא is rendered "came thronging to the king" in 6:7, and דָת לְמָדַי וּפָרַס "the law of Media and Persia" in 6:9 and 6:13.

old: The meaning of the rare Aramaic noun dachawan is uncertain; it is most commonly rendered "entertainment" or "diversions," though proposals include "musical instruments," "concubines," or "food."
new: The meaning of the rare Aramaic noun dachawan is uncertain; proposals include "entertainment," "diversions," "musical instruments," "concubines," or "food."
reason: Removes a claim about how translations commonly render דַחֲוָן, keeping the lexical uncertainty.

old: In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, from the lineage of Media, who was made king over the kingdom of the Chaldeans,
new: In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, from the seed of Media, who was made king over the kingdom of the Chaldeans,
reason: The Hebrew מִזֶּרַע מָדָי (zera, offspring sense) takes the edition's standard rendering "seed".

old: So I set my face toward the Lord God to seek Him in prayer and supplications, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.
new: So I set my face toward the Lord God to seek by prayer and supplications, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.
reason: לְבַקֵּשׁ תְּפִלָּה וְתַחֲנוּנִים has no object pronoun; "Him" is supplied without Hebrew basis.

old: After the sixty-two weeks, an anointed one will be cut off, and there will be nothing for him; and the people of the coming prince will destroy the city and the sanctuary. Its end will be with a flood, and until the end there will be war; desolations are decreed.
new: After the sixty-two weeks, an anointed one will be cut off, and there will be nothing for him; and the people of the coming prince will destroy the city and the sanctuary. Its end will be with a flood, and until the end of the war desolations are decreed.
reason: In MT וְעַד קֵץ מִלְחָמָה נֶחֱרֶצֶת שֹׁמֵמוֹת the conjunctive accent joins קֵץ to מִלְחָמָה ("until the end of war"), and there is no separate clause "there will be war".

old: And he will confirm a strong covenant with the many for one week, and for half of the week he will cause sacrifice and grain offering to cease; and upon the wing of abominations will be a desolator, until the decreed complete destruction is poured out upon the desolator."
new: And he will make a covenant strong with the many for one week, and for half of the week he will cause sacrifice and grain offering to cease; and upon the wing of abominations will be a desolator, until the decreed complete destruction is poured out upon the desolator."
reason: וְהִגְבִּיר בְּרִית means "he will make a covenant strong"; the strength belongs to the verb, and "confirm a strong covenant" both doubles it and moves it onto the noun.

old: Yet the prince of the kingdom of Persia stood opposing me for twenty-one days; then look, Michael, one of the foremost princes, came to help me, since I had been left there beside the kings of Persia.
new: Yet the prince of the kingdom of Persia stood opposing me for twenty-one days; then look, Michael, one of the foremost princes, came to help me, and I was left there beside the kings of Persia.
reason: וַאֲנִי נוֹתַרְתִּי שָׁם is a coordinate clause ("and I was left there"); "since" invents a causal link to Michael's help.

old: Now I will tell you the truth. Look, three more kings will arise for Persia, and the fourth will acquire far greater wealth than all of them; and when he grows strong through his wealth, he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
new: Now I will tell you the truth. Look, three more kings will arise for Persia, and the fourth will acquire greater wealth than all of them; and when he grows strong through his wealth, he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
reason: יַעֲשִׁיר עֹשֶׁר־גָּדוֹל מִכֹּל is "will become rich with great wealth beyond all"; "far" is an unwarranted intensifier.

old: Masoretic vocalization reads ha-yoldah (Qal active participle with 3fs suffix), "the one who fathered her," rather than "her child"; likewise "his arm" translates the MT text (uzero'o) rather than an emendation to "his offspring."
new: Masoretic vocalization reads ha-yoldah (Qal active participle with 3fs suffix), "the one who fathered her," rather than "her child"; likewise "his arm" translates the MT text (uzero'o) rather than an emendation to "his seed" (zar'o).
reason: Note updated to match the standard rendering "seed" for זַרְעוֹ, the emended reading it mentions.

old: In a time of tranquility he will enter the richest parts of the province, and he will do what neither his fathers nor his fathers' fathers did: he will scatter plunder, spoil, and goods among them. He will also devise his schemes against fortified places, yet only for a time.
new: In a time of tranquility he will enter the richest parts of the province, and he will do what neither his fathers nor his fathers' fathers did: he will scatter plunder, spoil, and goods among them. He will also devise his schemes against fortified places, yet for a time.
reason: וְעַד־עֵת is simply "and until a time"; "only" has no Hebrew basis.

old: The opening clause places a construct noun directly before a finite Piel verb (tehillat dibber-YHWH, literally "the beginning of the LORD spoke"); the preposition be- ("through") can also mean "with" or "to."
new: The opening clause places a construct noun directly before a finite Piel verb (tehillat dibber followed by the divine name, literally "the beginning of the LORD spoke"); the preposition be- ("through") can also mean "with" or "to."
reason: Notes must not print YHWH; refer to "the divine name."

old: Ammi ("My people") and Ruhamah ("She has been shown compassion") reverse the names Lo-ammi and Lo-ruhamah from chapter 1. Masoretic Hosea 2:1-3 corresponds to 1:10-2:1 in many English Bibles.
new: Ammi ("My people") and Ruhamah ("She has been shown compassion") reverse the names Lo-ammi and Lo-ruhamah from chapter 1.
reason: Remove claim about what English Bibles do; the note's lexical content stands.

old: The Masoretic Text reads we'ammekha kimrivei khohen ("for your people are like those who dispute with a priest"), using a Hiphil masculine plural construct participle of riv; some modern versions emend the text to read "my dispute is with you, priest."
new: The Masoretic Text reads we'ammekha kimrivei khohen ("for your people are like those who dispute with a priest"), using a Hiphil masculine plural construct participle of riv; a conjectural emendation would read "my dispute is with you, priest."
reason: Replace claim about what modern versions do with a neutral description of the emendation.

old: The idiom shuv shevut ("restore the fortunes," literally "turn a turning" or "bring back the captivity") closes verse 11 in the Masoretic Text, though some modern versions attach this clause to 7:1.
new: The idiom shuv shevut ("restore the fortunes," literally "turn a turning" or "bring back the captivity") closes verse 11 in the Masoretic Text, though some interpreters attach this clause to 7:1.
reason: Replace claim about what modern versions do with a neutral statement.

old: A difficult verse in MT: telu'im (Qal passive participle of tala) literally means 'hung/suspended toward,' and yiqra'uhu ('they call him') with el-al ('to the Most High') and Polel yeromem ('exalt') is variously construed.
new: A difficult verse in MT: telu'im (Qal passive participle of tala) literally means 'hung/suspended toward,' and yiqra'uhu ('they call him') with el-al ('upward,' often understood as 'to the Most High') and Polel yeromem ('exalt') is variously construed.
reason: Align the note with the literal rendering of עַל.

old: And My people cling to turning away from Me; though they summon him to the Most High, not one at all will exalt Him.
new: And My people cling to turning away from Me; though they summon him upward, not one at all will exalt Him.
reason: Hebrew has אֶל־עַל ("upward/on high"), not עֶלְיוֹן; the same עַל is rendered "upward" in 7:16 with the "Most High" understanding left to the note.

old: Following the Masoretic vocalization, ke-shachar means "like dawn," picturing the swarm sweeping swiftly across the mountain ridges; some modern versions emend the vowels to ke-shechor ("like blackness").
new: Following the Masoretic vocalization, ke-shachar means "like dawn," picturing the swarm sweeping swiftly across the mountain ridges; repointing as ke-shechor would give "like blackness."
reason: Note should not describe what modern versions do; states the alternative pointing of כְּשַׁחַר neutrally.

old: Hebrew Masoretic numbering begins chapter 3 here (corresponding to 2:28-32 in most English Bibles); unlike the quotation in Acts 2:17, the Hebrew text reads simply achare-khen ("afterward") and et-ruchi ("My Spirit").
new: Hebrew Masoretic numbering begins chapter 3 here (corresponding to 2:28-32 in an alternative chapter division); unlike the quotation in Acts 2:17, the Hebrew text reads simply achare-khen ("afterward") and et-ruchi ("My Spirit").
reason: Removes a claim about what English Bibles do; the numbering fact is kept neutrally.

old: those who trample the head of the weak into the dust of the earth and turn aside the way of the afflicted; and a man and his father go to the same young woman, so as to profane My holy name.
new: those who trample the head of the weak into the dust of the earth and turn aside the way of the afflicted; and a man and his father go to the young woman, so as to profane My holy name.
reason: Hebrew has only אֶל־הַנַּעֲרָה "to the young woman"; "same" is an interpretive addition.

old: "For on the day I bring punishment upon Israel for its transgressions, I will also bring punishment upon the altars of Bethel; and the horns of the altar will be hacked off and fall to the ground.
new: "For on the day I bring punishment upon Israel for its transgressions, I will bring punishment upon the altars of Bethel; and the horns of the altar will be hacked off and fall to the ground.
reason: וּפָקַדְתִּי is a plain weqatal apodosis with no גַּם; "also" has no Hebrew basis.

old: In the Masoretic Hebrew versification followed here, 2:1-11 corresponds to 1:17-2:10 in most English Bibles.
new: In the Masoretic Hebrew versification followed here, 2:1-11 corresponds to 1:17-2:10 in an alternative versification.
reason: Removes a claim about what English Bibles do while keeping the numbering fact.

old: Hebrew meshamerim (the sole Piel occurrence of shamar in the Hebrew Bible) paired with havlei-shav (literally "vanities of emptiness," a poetic idiom for false gods) contrasts idol worship with "their steadfast love" (chasdam), which can mean either their own loyalty or the faithful love God extends to them.
new: Hebrew meshamerim (the sole Piel occurrence of shamar in the Hebrew Bible) paired with havlei-shav (literally "vanities of emptiness," a poetic idiom for false gods) contrasts idol worship with "their loyal love" (chasdam), which can mean either their own loyalty or the loyal love God extends to them.
reason: Updates the note to match the verse, where chasdam is now rendered "their loyal love."

old: Those who pay heed to worthless vanities abandon their steadfast love.
new: Those who pay heed to worthless vanities abandon their loyal love.
reason: Hebrew chasdam ("their hesed") is the noun hesed, standardized to "loyal love" as elsewhere in the edition.

old: He prayed to the LORD and said, "Please, LORD, was this not my word while I was still on my own soil? For this reason I acted beforehand to flee to Tarshish, for I knew that You are a God who is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and great in faithful love, and relenting over the calamity.
new: He prayed to the LORD and said, "Please, LORD, was this not my word while I was still on my own soil? For this reason I acted beforehand to flee to Tarshish, for I knew that You are a God who is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and great in loyal love, and relenting over the calamity.
reason: Hebrew werav-chesed ("and great in hesed") is the noun hesed, standardized to "loyal love" as elsewhere in the edition.

old: And they will sit, each person beneath his vine and beneath his fig tree, and there will be no one to frighten them; for the mouth of the LORD of armies has spoken.
new: And they will sit, each person beneath his vine and beneath his fig tree, and there will be no one to frighten them; for the mouth of the LORD of hosts has spoken.
reason: יְהֹוָה צְבָאוֹת is rendered "the LORD of hosts" throughout the edition.

old: He has declared to you, mortal, what is good; and what is the LORD requiring from you except to practice justice, to love steadfast kindness, and to walk in humility with your God?
new: He has declared to you, mortal, what is good; and what is the LORD requiring from you except to practice justice, to love loyal love, and to walk in humility with your God?
reason: Hebrew we'ahavat chesed ("and to love hesed") has the noun hesed, standardized to "loyal love"; the repeated "love" mirrors the Hebrew verb-object pair and is kept for consistency.

old: The MT vocalizes the verb as Qal imperfect ("Can I be pure?"), expressing either a rhetorical question from the merchant's standpoint or the LORD's refusal to remain blameless while tolerating fraud; many translators repoint it as Piel ("Can I acquit?").
new: The MT vocalizes the verb as Qal imperfect ("Can I be pure?"), expressing either a rhetorical question from the merchant's standpoint or the LORD's refusal to remain blameless while tolerating fraud; it can also be repointed as Piel ("Can I acquit?").
reason: Removes a claim about what translators do; keeps the grammatical alternative.

old: Ketiv reads wgdwl (plene), while Qere reads ugedol-koach (defective construct form before maqqef, "great in strength"); both carry the same meaning. The Masoretic atnach divides the verse after yenaqqeh, placing the second YHWH at the start of the second half as casus pendens ("The LORD—His path is...").
new: Ketiv reads wgdwl (plene), while Qere reads ugedol-koach (defective construct form before maqqef, "great in strength"); both carry the same meaning. The Masoretic atnach divides the verse after yenaqqeh, placing the second occurrence of the divine name at the start of the second half as casus pendens ("The LORD—His path is...").
reason: Notes must not print the divine name as YHWH; say "the divine name".

old: The burden renders Hebrew massa, literally a lifting up or burden, used as a technical term for a weighty prophetic pronouncement or oracle.
new: Pronouncement renders Hebrew massa, literally a lifting up or burden, used as a technical term for a weighty prophetic pronouncement or oracle.
reason: Note updated to match the harmonized rendering of massa.

old: The burden that Habakkuk the prophet saw.
new: The pronouncement that Habakkuk the prophet saw.
reason: massa as a book/oracle heading is rendered "pronouncement" in Nahum 1:1 and Malachi 1:1; align the same Hebrew term.

old: We will not die follows the Masoretic Hebrew (lo namut), which traditional scribal notes (tiqqun sopherim) identify as safeguarding reverent speech alongside the sense You do not die.
new: We will not die follows the Masoretic Hebrew (lo namut); rabbinic tradition lists it among the tiqqune sopherim (scribal corrections), holding that it replaced an original "You do not die."
reason: Clarifies the garbled description of the tiqqun sopherim tradition for lo namut.

old: Puffed up renders the 3fs Pual perfect 'uppela, agreeing with feminine naphsho (his soul). By his faithfulness translates be'emunato, denoting steadfast fidelity and trust (quoted in the New Testament as by faith).
new: Puffed up renders the 3fs Pual perfect 'uppela, agreeing with feminine naphsho (his soul). By his faithfulness translates be'emunato, denoting steadfast fidelity and trust.
reason: Removes a New Testament reference from a note on בֶּאֱמוּנָתוֹ.

old: GOD the Lord reflects the reversed Masoretic divine title YHWH 'adonay, in which the Tetragrammaton is pointed with the vowels of 'elohim before 'adonay.
new: GOD the Lord reflects the Masoretic order of the divine name followed by 'adonay (the reverse of the usual 'adonay plus the divine name); the divine name is pointed here with the vowels of 'elohim.
reason: Notes must not print YHWH/Tetragrammaton; refer to "the divine name".

old: Masoretic bemalkam literally reads "by their king," widely understood as a vocalization referring to the Ammonite deity Milcom (also spelled Malcam).
new: Masoretic bemalkam reads "by their king," probably alluding to the Ammonite god Milcom, whose name the Syriac and Vulgate read here.
reason: Note rewritten to match the literal rendering of the Masoretic pointing.

old: and those who bow down on the rooftops to the host of the heavens, and those who bow down, who swear to the LORD and swear by Milcom,
new: and those who bow down on the rooftops to the host of the heavens, and those who bow down, who swear to the LORD and swear by their king,
reason: MT בְּמַלְכָּם is pointed "by their king"; "Milcom" follows the Syriac/Vulgate reading rather than the Hebrew as it stands.

new: Hebrew we'en-'etkhem 'elay is verbless (literally "and there was not you to Me"); "turn back" supplies the implied sense (compare Amos 4:9).
reason: The verb "turn back" has no counterpart in the Hebrew; a note discloses the supplied sense.

old: Hebrew ha-satan ("the Accuser" or "the Adversary," traditionally rendered "Satan") carries the definite article as a courtroom title and forms a cognate wordplay with the Qal infinitive construct lesitno ("to accuse him").
new: Hebrew ha-satan ("the Accuser" or "the Adversary") carries the definite article as a courtroom title and forms a cognate wordplay with the Qal infinitive construct lesitno ("to accuse him").
reason: Translator note should describe the Hebrew, not English translation tradition; the note explains הַשָּׂטָן as a titled noun with the article.

old: Hebrew tsemach ("Branch" or "Sprout") lacks the definite article and functions here as a messianic title or proper name (cf. 6:12).
new: Hebrew tsemach ("Branch" or "Sprout") lacks the definite article and functions here as a title or proper name (cf. 6:12).
reason: Notes should not make doctrinal assertions ("messianic"); the Hebrew itself only uses tsemach without the article.

old: Thus has the LORD of hosts spoken, saying, "Judge with true justice, and practice loyal love and compassion, each man with his brother.
new: This is what the LORD of hosts has said, saying, "Judge with true justice, and practice loyal love and compassion, each man with his brother.
reason: כֹּה אָמַר יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת is 'This is what the LORD of hosts says/has said' throughout the edition.

old: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "I am zealous for Zion with great zeal, and with great fury I am zealous for her."
new: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "I am jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and with great fury I am jealous for her."
reason: Identical Hebrew qinne'ti ... qin'ah gedolah is rendered "jealous ... jealousy" in 1:14 (and qin'ah as "jealousy" in Nahum/Zephaniah).

old: An oracle: the word of the LORD is against the land of Hadrach, and Damascus is its resting place, for the eye of mankind and of all the tribes of Israel is toward the LORD,
new: A pronouncement: the word of the LORD is against the land of Hadrach, and Damascus is its resting place, for the eye of mankind and of all the tribes of Israel is toward the LORD,
reason: massa heading rendered "pronouncement" as in Nahum 1:1 and Malachi 1:1.

old: The Masoretic Text clearly reads hayyotser (Qal participle of yatsar, "the potter"). Some ancient versions and modern translations emend to ha'otsar ("the treasury"), which departs from the Hebrew text.
new: The Masoretic Text clearly reads hayyotser (Qal participle of yatsar, "the potter"). Some ancient versions (e.g. the Syriac) reflect ha'otsar ("the treasury") instead.
reason: Remove the claim about what modern translations do; keep a neutral ancient-version comparison.

old: The oracle of the word of the LORD concerning Israel—the declaration of the LORD, who stretches out the heavens, founds the earth, and forms the spirit of man within him:
new: The pronouncement of the word of the LORD concerning Israel—the declaration of the LORD, who stretches out the heavens, founds the earth, and forms the spirit of man within him:
reason: massa heading rendered "pronouncement" as in Nahum 1:1 and Malachi 1:1.

old: Hebrew ben yadekha literally means "between your hands," an idiom likely referring to the chest or upper back; me'ahavay is a Piel participle of ahav ("those who love me," often rendered "my friends" or "my lovers").
new: Hebrew ben yadekha literally means "between your hands," an idiom likely referring to the chest or upper back; me'ahavay is a Piel participle of ahav ("those who love me").
reason: Translator note should describe the Hebrew, not English translation tradition; מְאַהֲבָי is glossed literally.
